item.title: Peoria, Normal principals up for Golden Apple Leadership Award
item.description: Fabian Daniels and Angie Codron, principals from Peoria and Normal schools respectively, are among the seven finalists for the Golden Apple Award for Excellence in Leadership, which recognizes exemplary school leaders who have had a significant and sustained positive impact on their schools.

item.title: What's On your Table? | Ep. 14: Fairways
item.description: Fairways, a new restaurant in Peoria, Illinois, offers a variety of low-country cuisine with a golf flair, and is designed to be inclusive to people of all ages and budgets.

item.title: Dow drops 400 after trimming an early plunge of 1,200 as oil prices climb even higher
item.description: NEW YORK (AP) — A sell-off for stocks wrapped around the world and hit Wall Street Tuesday, while oil prices climbed even higher on worries about the widening war with Iran. item.title: Laura Sniff wins 2026 Remarkable Woman for advocacy work for the disabled
item.description: Laura Sniff has been working for over two decades to eliminate the stigma surrounding disabilities, and has created two non-profits, Blue Ridge Community Farm and the Picket Fence, to provide educational experiences and employment opportunities for disabled people.

item.title: Misuse of less than 'five figures' led to dismissal of PHA's finance officer
item.description: The Peoria Housing Authority held a press conference to discuss the termination of their Chief Financial Officer and the resignation of their former CEO, both of which were unrelated incidents and are currently under investigation by the Peoria Police Department.

item.title: ISU and HCC strengthen partnership with new articulation agreements
item.description: Heartland Community College and Illinois State University have signed three new articulation agreements to streamline the transfer process for students pursuing degrees in special education, engineering, and mechanical engineering.

item.title: Peoria man faces new charge for allegedly severely injuring his infant son
item.description: A 20-year-old North Valley man faces an additional felony count for allegedly severely injuring his infant son, who suffered severe head trauma in December while in his care.

item.title: Local art on display in Peoria City Hall
item.description: The Public Arts Advisory Commission (PAAC) in Peoria, Illinois has been hosting an art exhibit in the mayor's suite since 2022, featuring 43 pieces from local artists this year, ranging from paintings to mixed media.

item.title: Early wins at the bridge: Residents reconnect with jobs & services
item.description: Home Sweet Home Ministries' "The Bridge" has been open for two months and residents are seeing progress in reconnecting with services, employment, and making steps towards permanent housing, though some are struggling with mental health and sobriety.

item.title: The Illinois battle for affordable home insurance rates
item.description: Gov. JB Pritzker is pushing for an insurance bill to reduce homeowners insurance costs in Illinois, while State Rep. Sharon Chung is trying to negotiate a bill that balances affordability with the needs of local businesses.
